tts: A pharmacy syrup became the most recognized drink on Earth, and the unofficial taste of Christmas. How did that happen?
In eighteen eighty-six, pharmacist John Pemberton in Atlanta cooked up a syrup to mix with soda water. In the first year, it sold about nine glasses a day.
Businessman Asa Candler bought the formula, and in eighteen ninety-nine the bottling rights were sold for just one dollar.
In nineteen fifteen came the curvy bottle, designed so you could recognize it by touch, even in the dark.
There was a famous flop, too: in nineteen eighty-five, they changed the recipe, people were furious, and seventy-nine days later the old Coke was back.

And Christmas? That's thanks to artist Haddon Sundblom. Starting in nineteen thirty-one, he painted a warm, chubby Santa in red for Coke's ads. The red suit existed before, but these ads made him the Santa the whole world knows.
In nineteen ninety-five came the glowing trucks and the jingle Holidays Are Coming. The ad aired in more than a hundred countries, and for many people, it's when the holidays officially start.
Today, people drink about two billion servings of its drinks every single day. And it all started with nine glasses in a pharmacy.
